$comment: The expo-updates fingerprints of the binaries currently in users' hands.
An `eas update` only reaches a build whose fingerprint matches exactly;
publishing to any other value reports success and reaches zero devices,
with no error anywhere. scripts/verify-ota-target.mjs compares the working
tree against this file and refuses to publish on a mismatch.
Update this file in the same commit that ships a new binary, and never to
silence the preflight — a mismatch means the update cannot land, not that
"setAside" lists files that landed on main after that binary was built and
only touch another platform's native code. scripts/publish-ota.mjs removes
them from its throwaway tree before fingerprinting that platform, so JS from
main still reaches the binary. Drop the list when that platform ships a new
binary. This file is not a fingerprint input, so editing it never moves one.

android.$note: Built from main 26c017bd (EAS build 010bc000, workflow run 36534158551) for the Google Play policy notice (Sexual Content / AI-Generated Content, fix by 2026-10-05): the server-side prompt gate from 0e903fde and Android's covered NSFW posts (26c017bd). Its runtime is the same 02b8fe85 as 0.1.8 (76), built from 5837720a, so every update published at this fingerprint reaches both builds and nothing about OTA reach changed. Closed alpha and production were both approved and published on 2026-09-29 with full rollout (managed publishing is off). 76 is only whatever has not updated yet.

ios.$note: Built from main 5837720a (#225; EAS build 07f8b038, workflow run 36322017759) and uploaded to TestFlight for the internal group 2026-09-27. It is the first binary with the native menus (#217, @expo/ui). EAS recorded this runtime for the build, and a clean npm ci of main 015fd701 fingerprints the same. Submitted to App Review as version 0.1.8 on 2026-09-27 (automatic release on approval), in place of 0.1.7 (57), which was withdrawn from review and never released. Hold iOS updates while it is in review, so the reviewer sees the build as submitted. Until Apple approves it, the App Store still serves 0.1.5 (54) at 835877cfddddf3644cf2e03bc8da01d7aec206d0, which no update from main can reach, so an update published against this fingerprint reaches TestFlight only.
